# PLTR Q2 2026 pre-research record

## Scope and completed method

This package covers only event 2026-08-03-pltr, the scheduled AMC Q2 2026 disclosure, with a hard information cutoff of 2026-08-02T10:40:21.0414058Z. It selects only PLTRUSDT-PERP.BINANCE. It contains no live-price, K-line, liquidity, sizing, watcher, or execution judgment.

The prior research was continued rather than mechanically reformatted. Three independent roles re-examined the financial ladder, issuer-specific earnings reactions, and the risk of making HOLD either dominant or unreachable. Their common conclusion was that the old all-fields BUY/SELL chains were too conservative, while a simple beat of Palantir's company guidance was too weak to justify a trade. The adjudicated policy therefore scores six definition-locked evidence blocks and reserves HOLD for ordinary, materially mixed, or non-comparable disclosures.

## Decisive baselines and expectation problem

The official Q2 guide is revenue $1.797-$1.801bn and adjusted operating income (AOI) $1.063-$1.067bn. The Q1-issued FY26 baselines are revenue $7.650-$7.662bn, AOI $4.440-$4.452bn, U.S. commercial revenue above $3.224bn and at least 120% growth, and adjusted FCF $4.2-$4.4bn. Q1 U.S. commercial and government revenue were $0.595bn and $0.687bn. [S1]

Company guidance has recently been conservative. Calculated against the immediately preceding company guide upper bound, Q2 2025, Q3 2025, Q4 2025, and Q1 2026 revenue exceeded by approximately 7.0%, 8.7%, 5.7%, and 6.3%; AOI exceeded by approximately 14.7%, 20.8%, 14.2%, and 12.5%. [S1][S3][S4][S5][S6] Consequently, merely clearing $1.801bn revenue and $1.067bn AOI is not a strong surprise.

Public expectation pages conflict, but the high bar is real. A named analyst's 84%-85% total growth view implies about $1.85bn revenue from the Q2 2025 base, and 135% U.S. commercial growth implies about $0.719bn. Other public snapshots ranged materially and were not definition-complete. The policy therefore does not call any one page consensus; it embeds the robust high-expectation region in the R/O/S bands and requires forward incremental evidence for a directional trade. [S3][S7][S8][S9]

## Six-block operating model

The first-minute agent calculates R, O, S, H, F, and Q exactly as locked in analysis_brief. R measures revenue against the pre-researched market and company range. O jointly measures AOI and adjusted margin. S compresses U.S. commercial and government breadth. H removes the realized Q2 variance from the new FY revenue and AOI guides, so a mechanical pass-through raise is neutral. F combines Q3 continuation and the FY U.S. commercial floor. Q confirms GAAP and cash quality but cannot create a trade by itself.

R, O, H, and F are the core drivers. A simultaneous +2 and -2 among those four is a material conflict and maps to HOLD even if secondary points produce a non-zero total. S and Q may confirm, weaken, or create a conflict, but cannot substitute for current results and forward information. Optional TCV, RDV, RPO, deal counts, and customer counts do not gate any tier. A disclosed accounting or collectibility problem is a HOLD only when it destroys comparability or reliability; an economically quantified deterioration that remains comparable is negative evidence rather than an automatic veto. [S1][S2][S3]

The H neutral band is widened from the old $1m disclosure-precision threshold to economically meaningful thresholds. The Q3 test uses absolute revenue and margin ranges informed by the prior FY path and Q3 2025 comparison, rather than requiring Q3 midpoint to exceed an unusually strong Q2 actual. This removes the old paradox in which a larger Q2 beat made a positive classification harder. [S1][S4]

## Historical price-reaction calibration

The fixed window is the AMC release-day regular-session close to the next trading-day close. SEC acceptance times identify the AMC sample; Yahoo Finance unadjusted daily closes supply both endpoints. The 2023-11-02 BMO release was excluded. [S10][S11][S12]

Thirteen comparable AMC reactions from Q4 2022 through Q1 2026 were: +21.2%, +23.4%, -5.3%, +30.8%, -15.1%, +10.4%, +23.5%, +24.0%, -12.0%, +7.8%, -7.9%, +6.8%, and -6.9%. The absolute median was 12.1%; the latest six absolute moves had a median near 7.9% and mean near 10.9%. Earlier 20%-31% upside repricings occurred in a different adoption and valuation regime and are down-weighted. The latest sequence is more relevant: Q2 2025 +7.8%, Q3 2025 -7.9%, Q4 2025 +6.8%, and Q1 2026 -6.9%, despite every disclosure being strong in company-guide terms. [S1][S3][S4][S5][S6][S12]

This evidence sets a no-action expected-impact band of -4% to +4%. Weak is calibrated at 6% on either side, medium at 10% upside and 11% downside, and strong at 16% upside and 18% downside. Strong downside is an explicit tail extrapolation because the sample contains no full operating breakdown. Percentages represent the complete event repricing; NT later measures movement already realized and remaining space.

## Candidate causality and rejected spillovers

PLTRUSDT-PERP.BINANCE is retained because the disclosure directly changes the issuer's revenue, profitability, cash generation, and forward plan, and Binance provides the exact PLTR-linked eligible instrument. Index and basis behavior remains an NT concern. [S16]

No other software, cloud, defense, semiconductor, or AI instrument has a quantified, sign-stable, short-horizon transmission path. Product cadence, NGC2 validation, and the Army agreement support PLTR's operating context but do not identify another issuer whose earnings must move in the same direction; contract ceilings are not funded obligations. Sovereignty risk is relevant to PLTR's international government trajectory but also does not create a separate candidate. [S13][S14][S15][S17]

## Debate adjudication and completeness

The financial role proposed six auditable blocks so neutral secondary evidence no longer kills a valid medium or weak signal. The price-impact role showed that strong official results can still produce negative closes and calibrated 13 issuer-specific AMC reactions. The critic rejected both the old approximately all-HOLD design and a permissive rule that buys every company-guide beat. The final ladder keeps ordinary habitual beats with neutral forward revisions in HOLD, permits weak SELL even when results remain above conservative company guidance, and requires broad core agreement only for strong tiers.

All seven outcomes are reachable and mutually resolved by priority, total score, core-driver signs, and the explicit HOLD conflict rule. Core fields, definitions, missing-field behavior, calculations, comparison bands, percentage calibration, candidate selection, and falsifiers are locked. No disclosure-time research, browsing, price interpretation, or additional policy judgment remains.
analysis_brief:
# PLTR Q2 2026 first-minute calculation sheet

Use only the first complete official disclosure package. Do not browse, inspect prices, or wait for a call or later filing.

## Required fields

Extract the reporting period, units, Q2 revenue, Q2 AOI and adjusted margin, U.S. commercial revenue, U.S. government revenue, Q3 revenue and AOI guide ranges, new FY26 revenue and AOI guide ranges, new FY26 U.S. commercial amount and growth floors, GAAP operating margin, CFO, capex, adjusted FCF and adjusted-FCF margin. Revenue, AOI, both U.S. segments, Q3 revenue/AOI guidance, and FY revenue/AOI guidance are core fields. If any core field is absent or definition-incomparable, classification is HOLD. Missing GAAP/cash details make Q=0 if no reliability problem is disclosed. TCV, RDV, RPO, deal counts, customers, and NDR are optional and do not affect the score.

All monetary values below are USD billions.

## Locked baselines

Q2 revenue guide 1.797-1.801. Q2 AOI guide 1.063-1.067. Old FY revenue midpoint 7.656. Old FY AOI midpoint 4.446. Old FY U.S. commercial floor 3.224 and growth floor 120%. Old FY adjusted-FCF midpoint 4.300. Q1 U.S. commercial 0.595 and U.S. government 0.687. Q2 2025 comparators: revenue 1.003697 and U.S. commercial 0.306.

## Score R: Q2 revenue

R=+2 if revenue >=1.900; +1 if 1.840<=revenue<1.900; 0 if 1.780<=revenue<1.840; -1 if 1.720<=revenue<1.780; -2 if revenue<1.720.

## Score O: AOI and adjusted margin

O=+2 if AOI>=1.170 and adjusted margin>=61.5%. Otherwise O=+1 if AOI>=1.100 and adjusted margin>=59.5%. O=-2 if AOI<0.930 or adjusted margin<54.0%. Otherwise O=-1 if AOI<1.020 and adjusted margin<57.0%. All other internally neutral or mixed combinations give O=0.

## Score S: U.S. segment breadth

First score U.S. commercial C: +2 if >=0.735; +1 if 0.690-0.734999; 0 if 0.650-0.689999; -1 if 0.610-0.649999; -2 if <0.610.

Score U.S. government G: +2 if >=0.790; +1 if 0.745-0.789999; 0 if 0.690-0.744999; -1 if 0.650-0.689999; -2 if <0.650.

Compress them: S=+2 when C and G are both at least +1 and either is +2; S=+1 when both are non-negative and at least one is positive; S=0 when they have opposite signs or are both zero; S=-1 when both are non-positive and at least one is negative; S=-2 when both are at most -1 and either is -2.

## Score H: incremental H2 revision

Compute delta_h2_revenue = midpoint(new FY revenue guide) - 7.656 - (Q2 revenue - 1.799).

Compute delta_h2_aoi = midpoint(new FY AOI guide) - 4.446 - (Q2 AOI - 1.065).

H=+2 when both deltas exceed +0.050 and either revenue delta is at least +0.100 or AOI delta is at least +0.075. Otherwise H=+1 when both are non-negative and at least one exceeds +0.020. H=-2 when both are below -0.050 and either revenue delta is at most -0.100 or AOI delta is at most -0.075. Otherwise H=-1 when both are non-positive and at least one is below -0.020. All other small, pass-through-only, or opposite-sign combinations give H=0.

## Score F: Q3 and FY U.S. commercial

Compute Q3 revenue midpoint and Q3 implied adjusted margin = Q3 AOI midpoint / Q3 revenue midpoint.

F=+2 if Q3 revenue midpoint>=2.120, implied margin>=60.0%, and the new FY U.S. commercial growth floor>=130%. Otherwise F=+1 if Q3 revenue midpoint>=2.050, implied margin>=58.5%, the new FY U.S. commercial amount floor>=3.224, and its growth floor>=120%. F=-2 if Q3 revenue midpoint<1.900 and implied margin<54.0%, or if the new FY U.S. commercial growth floor<110%. Otherwise F=-1 if Q3 revenue midpoint<1.980, implied margin<56.5%, the FY U.S. commercial amount floor<3.224, or its growth floor<120%. All other neutral or internally mixed combinations give F=0.

## Score Q: GAAP and cash quality

Q=+1 only when GAAP operating margin>=45%, CFO-capex>0, and adjusted-FCF margin>=50%. Q=-1 if GAAP operating margin<38%, CFO-capex<=0, or adjusted-FCF margin<35%. Otherwise Q=0. Missing quality fields also give Q=0 unless the package discloses an unusable reconciliation or reliability problem.

## Classification inputs

Calculate T=R+O+S+H+F+Q. The core drivers are R, O, H, and F.

A hard HOLD applies when the issuer, period, units, or official version cannot be confirmed; any core field is missing or definition-incomparable; a material reclassification prevents comparison; the GAAP/non-GAAP reconciliation is unusable; a restatement, revenue-recognition, collectibility, or cancellation issue makes the package unreliable; or a material unforeseen fact invalidates this policy. A quantified negative fact that remains comparable is not a veto: reflect it in O, S, F, or Q.

An extreme core conflict exists when at least one of R/O/H/F equals +2 and another equals -2. Apply the candidate outcome table from strongest to weakest. If a hard HOLD or extreme core conflict applies, select HOLD regardless of T. Otherwise use T and the core-driver sign requirements exactly. Keep optional fields neutral.

STRONG_BUY.condition: No hard HOLD or extreme core conflict applies; the locked score T from analysis_brief is at least +8; none of the four core drivers R, O, H, and F is negative; and both forward drivers H and F are positive.

MEDIUM_BUY.condition: No hard HOLD or extreme core conflict applies; STRONG_BUY is not met; T is at least +5; at least two of the four core drivers R, O, H, and F are positive; and at least one forward driver H or F is positive.

WEAK_BUY.condition: No hard HOLD or extreme core conflict applies; neither stronger BUY tier is met; T is at least +2; at least one core driver is positive; and either H or F is positive or both current-result drivers R and O equal +2.

HOLD.condition: A hard HOLD or extreme core conflict defined in analysis_brief applies; T is between -1 and +1 inclusive; current and forward core drivers materially oppose each other without meeting a directional condition; or none of the six directional outcome conditions is met. An ordinary habitual company-guide beat with only pass-through or neutral forward revisions is HOLD.

WEAK_SELL.condition: No hard HOLD or extreme core conflict applies; neither stronger SELL tier is met; T is at most -2; at least one core driver is negative; and either H or F is negative or both current-result drivers R and O are negative.

MEDIUM_SELL.condition: No hard HOLD or extreme core conflict applies; STRONG_SELL is not met; T is at most -5; at least two of the four core drivers R, O, H, and F are negative; and at least one forward driver H or F is negative.

STRONG_SELL.condition: No hard HOLD or extreme core conflict applies; the locked score T from analysis_brief is at most -8; none of the four core drivers R, O, H, and F is positive; and both forward drivers H and F are negative.
